items.title: State variables and units
items.description: The homogeneous model has five material stocks, plus temperature when thermal response is finite. Time is measured in years.
equations: y = (p, X_A, X_M, C, r); for tau > 0 append T.
r = p_CH4/p_CO2.
For habitat quadrature: y = (p_j, X_Aj, X_Mj, C_j for j=1,...,N; r), with one shared temperature T when tau > 0.
H = 8766 h yr^-1 converts hourly physiological rates into annual derivatives.

parameters.meaning: Dissolved-H2-equivalent pressure; dissolved concentration is K_H p
Acetogen and hydrogenotrophic-methanogen dry biomass concentrations
Local acetate concentration; named A or acetate in some documentation/code
Surface temperature; local habitat temperature is T plus its prescribed offset
parameters.value: Dynamic for tau > 0; algebraic for tau = 0

items.notes: The paper does not use the older one-guild donor/biomass state or its parabolic growth law. Throughout this digest, i=A,M, (z)_+=max(z,0), and ell denotes demographic loss, distinguished from habitat exchange d.

items.title: Acetogen uptake and growth
items.description: The paper reference uses saturating uptake, with A. bakii temperature shapes transferred onto an inferred A. woodii absolute rate scale.
equations: mu_A = Y_A[q_A-m_A(T)]; dX_A/dt = H(mu_A-ell)X_A.
V_A(T) and K_A(T) are independently linearly interpolated between the six tabulated temperatures.

parameters.meaning: Kotsyurbenko et al. 2001 A. bakii assay capacities at those temperatures
Uptake half-saturation pressures at those temperatures
Peters et al. 1998 A. woodii maximum biomass-synthesis rate used in the scale closure

items.notes: 03b M1 is broadly consistent, but the absolute capacity is inferred, not a measured A. woodii q_max. The earlier first-order acetogen alternative q_A=s_A u_A/K_A is not the paper reference.

items.title: Methanogen uptake and growth
items.description: The reference methanogen uses the MSB temperature shape and saturating uptake.
equations: s_M(T) = gamma s_A30 V_M(T)/560.
mu_M = Y_M[q_M-m_M(T)]; dX_M/dt = H(mu_M-ell)X_M.
V_M(T) and K_M(T) are independently linearly interpolated between the six assay temperatures.

parameters.meaning: Kotsyurbenko et al. 2001 MSB assay capacities

items.notes: The reference gamma approximates the source culture-capacity ratio, not its dry-mass-specific ratio. Neither normalization establishes an assay-compatible absolute population uptake capacity. MSP is an earlier alternative, not the paper reference.

items.title: Break-even hydrogen and the temperature switch
items.description: Each requirement is the hydrogen pressure giving zero net population growth. The reference switch is solved from equality of requirements.
equations: Q_i(T) = m_i(T)+ell/Y_i.
R_i^*(T) = p_i^*(T)+K_i(T)Q_i(T)/[s_i(T)-Q_i(T)] when Q_i<s_i; otherwise R_i^*=infinity.
T_switch solves R_A^*(T_switch)=R_M^*(T_switch); it is not imposed in the population equations.
Outlet feasibility additionally requires R_i^* < p_atm+J/k_ex.

parameters.meaning: Reaction enthalpies used in the fixed-energy threshold law
Chosen cessation energies within the repository's source-supported brackets
Requirements independently recomputed from implemented equations
Requirements independently recomputed from implemented equations

items.notes: At 278 K acetogens require less hydrogen; at 283 K methanogens do. The 282.780105860 K crossing belongs to the earlier first-order acetogen alternative. Exact pinning at 281.53 K applies to the reference fixed chemistry, not every product-feedback or turnover setting.

items.title: Maintenance and the Tijhuis temperature transfer
items.description: A shared Arrhenius slope scales each group's substrate-maintenance demand.
equations: mu_i=Y_i(q_i-m_i); maintenance is substrate expenditure, separate from demographic loss ell.

parameters.meaning: A. woodii hydrogen-maintenance anchor derived from Peters et al. 1998 acetate maintenance
Reference methanogen maintenance; no matched cold-MSB calibration
Tijhuis et al. 1993 pooled energetic-maintenance activation energy transferred to H2 demand

items.notes: 03b correctly calls this a transferred correlation. The reported Tijhuis dataset spans 5–75 degrees C; even the 4-degree uptake endpoint is slightly outside that maintenance dataset.

items.title: Physiology below the uptake measurements
items.description: The paper reference uses the named constant_shape continuation from 277.15 K down to 273 K.
equations: m_i(T) and p_i^*(T) continue using their temperature-dependent laws.
Alternative continuation: E_i=R ln[V_i(10 degrees C)/V_i(4 degrees C)]/(1/277.15-1/283.15).
Alternative s_i(T)=s_i(277.15) exp[-E_i/R(1/T-1/277.15)], with K_i still frozen.
items.notes: 03b M1 rounds 277.15 K to 277 K. Constant_shape freezes capacity and affinity, not maintenance or cessation pressure. The alternative continuation changes the C06 methanogen-only control from 273.517 to 276.807 K, reducing the mixed-minus-control contrast from 8.02 to 4.73 K.

items.title: Hydrogen supply and atmospheric exchange
items.description: Hydrogen is supplied continuously and exchanges with a prescribed atmospheric reservoir through a fixed conductance.
equations: K_H dp/dt = H[J-q_A X_A-q_M X_M-k_ex(p-p_atm)].
P = t_CH4 c_atm Phi; c_atm = seconds_per_year/N_CO2.
Lifeless pressure p_0=p_atm+J/k_ex.
Exchange k_ex(p-p_atm) is signed: p_atm>p imports hydrogen from the reservoir.

parameters.meaning: Fixed dissolved-H2 storage coefficient from the 30-degree uptake assay
Donor supply expressed as CH4-equivalent surface flux; N_A is Avogadro's constant and V is habitat L per surface cm2

parameters.value: Reference 1e-6; proportional to Phi at fixed V

parameters.meaning: Hydrogen exchange conductance, not a first-order rate constant
Nominal donor potential, distinct from actual methane abundance

items.notes: C59 keeps the fixed-chemistry set point at 281.5348 K through 100 Pa. Its critical margins change 0.149→0.119 yr for f=0 and 1.103→1.185 yr for f=0.5. At 200 Pa the searched f=0.5 mixed state disappears. This is an imposed reservoir, not a photochemical atmospheric-H2 budget; imported hydrogen can supplement nominal Phi.

items.title: Acetate, biomass retention and methane routing
items.description: Acetate is an explicit local stock. Biomass synthesis retains reducing equivalents before catabolic products are calculated.
equations: mu_i=Y_i(q_i-m_i); U_i=H q_i X_i.
B_i=H a_i max(mu_i,0)X_i; F_i=U_i-B_i.
dC/dt=F_A/4-(k_rec+k_other)C.
k_rec=f/t_A; k_other=(1-f)/t_A.
Local methane production = F_M/4+k_rec C.
Biomass-associated export E_i=H a_i[ell+max(-mu_i,0)]X_i.
At steady state, F_i=H(Q_i-a_i ell)X_i: direct methanogenesis yields 1/4 mol CH4 per catabolic mol H2; the acetogen route yields f/4 after acetate removal.

parameters.meaning: Catabolic, biomass-synthesis, uptake and biomass-export H2-equivalent flows
parameters.value: Calculated from instantaneous stocks and rates

parameters.meaning: Hydrogen retained per synthesized acetogen biomass; 4 times Peters' acetate-equivalent coefficient
Same biomass-composition coefficient imposed on methanogens
Acetate-pool removal time for constant recycling
Fraction of acetate removal routed to methane
parameters.value: 0,0.5,0.9 in homogeneous maps; 0,0.5 in invasions and chemical dials

items.notes: The paper uses constant recycling. The older cold-limited recycling alternative is separate. Methane-producing acetate recyclers are prescribed chemistry, not a third population. Lost biomass is exported rather than automatically recycled into methane; f=1 therefore does not imply identical methane delivery per supplied H2.

items.title: Atmospheric methane inventory
items.description: The model converts local methane production into a shared atmospheric ratio and applies linear removal.
equations: dr/dt = chi[F_M/4+k_rec C]+c_atm Phi_abiotic-r/t_CH4.
chi=V N_A/N_CO2; c_atm=seconds_per_year/N_CO2.
N_air=p_s N_A/(M_air g 10^4); N_CO2=f_CO2 N_air; f_CO2=p_CO2/p_s.
For habitats, replace the local production bracket by its quadrature-weighted mean.

parameters.meaning: Earth-mass serpentinization estimate quoted by Arney et al. 2016
Effective habitat volume per planetary surface area

items.notes: 03b M3 correctly labels the 10000-year lifetime an assumption. The repository's conditional 6–19-kyr estimate is not an Arney case-specific measured lifetime. Identifying the column inventory ratio with surface CH4/CO2 also assumes well-mixed methane.

items.title: Arney case-B climate mapping
items.description: The climate target is piecewise linear through digitized Arney case-B vertices, with explicitly assumed extensions.
equations: For r<r_0: T_clim=T_0+(T_first-T_0)ln[1+max(r,0)/s]/ln(1+r_0/s).
For r>r_last: T_clim=T_last.
At the reference switch, r=0.195106875 and dT_clim/dr=-721.258 K per unit ratio.

parameters.meaning: Case-B interpolation vertices, ordered by methane ratio
Methane-free bridge temperature in the population reference

items.notes: 03b M3 should distinguish the extracted curve from the assumed bridge and plateau. The paper reference uses T_0=283 K, overriding the older README/default 265 K. Haze cooling is the negative-slope branch after the peak; the final extracted vertices include a small upturn.

items.title: Finite climate-response time
items.description: A first-order temperature state supplies the paper's thermal inertia.
equations: tau dT/dt=T_clim(r)-T.
For tau=0, T=T_clim(r) algebraically.
All temperature-dependent biological rates use actual T, or T plus the habitat offset, rather than T_clim when tau>0.

parameters.value: Main spectral grid 0,0.03,0.1,0.3,1,3,10,30,100,300,1000; crossing search through 10000

parameters.meaning: Equilibrium climate target supplied by the case-B mapping

items.notes: 03b M3 matches the implementation. Tau is an assumed response coefficient, not an empirically calibrated Archean ocean timescale. The separate two-layer diagnostic is not the paper's main thermal equation.

items.title: Four product chemistries and the acetate dial
items.description: Product feedback multiplies cessation thresholds; the product stocks remain dynamic in every chemistry.
equations: p_A^*=p_A0^*(T)[max(C,0)/C_ref]^(a/4); p_M^*=p_M0^*(T)[max(r,0)p_CO2/p_CH4ref]^(m/4), applying each multiplier only when its feedback is enabled.
Chemistry switches (a,m): fixed=(0,0), methane_only=(0,1), acetate_only=(1,0), products=(1,1).
D1: p_A^*=p_A0^*(T)(C/C_ref)^(kappa/4), p_M^*=p_M0^*(T). At kappa=0 the acetogen multiplier is explicitly 1.
For C>0: partial p_A^*/partial C = kappa p_A^*/(4C).
items.notes: 03b M4 is consistent. Kappa changes the acetate exponent, not recycling rate or growth directly. Fixed products means fixed product effects on thresholds, not fixed acetate or methane inventories. Concentration/pressure ratios approximate activities/fugacities at fixed reference pH and CO2.

items.title: Continuous habitat-temperature spread
items.description: Habitats have local hydrogen, biomass and acetate, with shared atmospheric methane and climate.
equations: delta is uniform on [-sigma,sigma]; T_local(delta)=T+delta.
Mean X_i = integral[-sigma,sigma] X_i(delta) ddelta/(2 sigma).
dX_i(delta)/dt=H X_i(delta){Y_i[q_i(p(delta),T+delta)-m_i(T+delta)]-ell}+d[Mean X_i-X_i(delta)].
Local hydrogen and acetate retain their homogeneous budgets; atmospheric methane receives the uniform mean of local methane production.
Quadrature: Mean X_i approximately sum_j w_j X_ij, sum_j w_j=1. An order-four Gauss-Legendre node on panel [a,b] has weight (b-a)w_GL/(4 sigma).

parameters.meaning: Uniform temperature half-width, not standard deviation
parameters.value: D2: 0.003,0.01,0.03,0.1,0.3,1, plus zero-spread controls; preceding C1 map: 1,3,6

parameters.meaning: Gauss-Legendre nodes per panel; initial support divided into four panels
Agreement of refined supply slopes and finite first-loss margins
parameters.value: Slopes within max(0.001 K,2%); finite margins within 2%; censored classifications agree

items.notes: Adaptive refinement bisects panels with acetogen-share logit range above one, including endpoint profile evaluations; doubling further bisects mixed panels. The full T±sigma support must remain within 273–303.15 K. Every reported D2 setting passes doubling; the independently derived characteristic method checks selected states, not every state as 03b M4 might imply.

items.title: Equilibria, continuation and the 42 pinned states
items.description: Equilibria satisfy all physical budgets; supply sensitivity is obtained by implicit differentiation. Positive graded branches are followed by continuation.
equations: F(y,T_clim(r);Phi)=0.
For homogeneous fixed/methane-only mixtures, solve R_A^*=R_M^*, then solve hydrogen and methane allocation balances for X_A,X_M and the acetate balance for C.
J_0=partial F/partial y after substituting T_clim(r); v=-J_0^(-1)F_lnPhi.
S=dT^*/d ln Phi=T_clim'(r^*)v_r.
S_0 is the separate derivative with local guild biomass fractions frozen; G_loc=S/S_0 where defined.

parameters.meaning: Chemistries contributing the exactly pinned C54 states
Recycling fractions in the homogeneous scan
Operational criterion in the frontier recount

parameters.value: Implicit derivative, not a finite e-fold perturbation

items.notes: The 42 are roots, not 42 parameter combinations. Per chemistry: f=0 contributes 11 roots—three each at ell=.0005/.001 and five at .002, where P=.30/.36 each have greenhouse and cooling roots. f=.5 contributes eight—three each at .0005/.001 and two at .002, P=.30/.36. f=.9 contributes two—P=.24 at ell=.0005/.001. Six greenhouse roots are unstable at zero lag; the remaining 36 have finite first losses. Other missing branches are finite-search outcomes.

items.title: Linear stability and the first-loss margin
items.description: The critical response time is the first detected stable-to-unstable spectral crossing, with later recoveries retained.
equations: Let A=F_y at fixed T, b=F_T, c^T=T_clim'(r)e_r^T, where e_r selects atmospheric methane.
J_0=A+bc^T.
J_tau=[[A,b],[c^T/tau,-1/tau]].
Characteristic equation: (1+tau lambda)det(lambda I-A)-c^T adj(lambda I-A)b=0.
tau_c is the first detected crossing of max Re eigenvalue(J_tau) from negative to positive; lambda has units yr^-1.
For spatial states, independent elimination of local habitat blocks gives a four-variable characteristic determinant in mean A biomass, mean M biomass, methane and temperature.

parameters.meaning: Requested grid supplemented by a logarithmic search
parameters.value: 29 logarithmic points from 0.001 to 10000, combined with the main lag grid

parameters.meaning: Threshold distinguishing stable, neutral and already unstable states
Largest finite margin among the 36 initially stable pinned roots

items.notes: 03b R2's 0.15-year reference must specify f=0; default f=.5 gives 1.10 years. 'About 7 years or less' is more precisely 7.08 years. No loss detected through 10000 years is right-censored, not infinite stability. This thermal-state model is an ODE, not a fixed time-delay equation.

items.title: Perturbed mixed-state trajectories
items.description: Five homogeneous fixed-product trajectories test nonlinear consequences of unstable thermal response.
equations: X_A(0)=X_A^* exp(0.001); X_M(0)=X_M^*; remaining stocks and T start at their mixed equilibrium.
The exact kick is Delta ln X_A=0.001, equivalent to a 0.10005% biomass increase.
Global count N_i=X_i V_global/m_cell; minima retain logarithmic values even after physical floating-point underflow.

parameters.meaning: Adaptive stiff/nonstiff solver in positive coordinates
parameters.value: LSODA; census disabled; nominal samples every year

parameters.meaning: Acetogen and methanogen minima across 30000 years

items.notes: 03b R3 is supported over the stated horizon: neither group crosses one cell at f=0,tau=1; both cross below one in each tested 10/100-year case. These uncensored trajectories report temperature extrema, late-window spans, dense population minima and first one-cell crossings. They do not establish an attracting limit cycle or indefinite persistence. The 1-year case uses f=0.

items.title: The 24 invasion experiments
items.description: Each invasion begins at a conditional single-group equilibrium, with a prescribed dose of the missing group and no subsequent immigration.
equations: Design count = 2 directions x 2 chemistries x 2 recycling fractions x 3 response times = 24.
V_global=V A_eff; N_i=X_i V_global/m_cell.
At scheduled ten-year censuses, set an entire guild to zero if its global count is below one; absence is absorbing without immigration.
Resident equilibrium is calculated with the other guild disabled; introduce the missing guild at X_seed=1e-12 gDW L^-1.

parameters.value: Acetogen into methanogen; methanogen into acetogen

parameters.meaning: Invader dose, approximately 1.525e17 assumed global cells
Dry mass per cell for both groups

parameters.value: 10 yr; 1 cell, equivalent to 6.5573e-30 gDW L^-1

items.notes: 03b M6's 'closed habitat' should mean no cell immigration: hydrogen supply/exchange and methane loss remain active. The dose is not one cell. Separate uncensored and census runs support C52: all displaced residents cross below one; all 12 A-into-M census runs finish A-only, and all 12 reverse runs M-only. These are deterministic finite-rule endpoints, not coupled stochastic survival probabilities.

items.title: Demographic loss and growth yields
items.description: Constant true yields convert uptake minus maintenance into biomass synthesis; demographic loss is added once.
equations: mu_i=Y_i(q_i-m_i); net growth per year = H(mu_i-ell).
For branching diagnostics: birth_i=H max(mu_i,0); death_i=H[ell+max(-mu_i,0)].
Source assimilation conversion: Y_A,converted=1/[4(1/7.7+0.0206)]=1.661459, but the implemented reference retains reported Y_A=1.7.

parameters.meaning: Peters et al. 1998 maintenance-corrected A. woodii yield transferred to the acetogen
Representative transferred methanogen yield; no matched MSB temperature calibration

items.notes: Neither ell nor the methanogen yield is a calibrated Archean demographic parameter. Earlier standalone physiology sweeps used ell=0.0001,0.001,0.01 h^-1; those are not the narrower paper stability grid. Maintenance must not be described as this demographic loss.

items.title: Numerical settings and relevant verification
items.description: Existing tests and independent audits cover physical budgets, equilibrium algebra, derivatives, thermal spectra, positive-coordinate trajectories and finite censuses. Tests were inspected, not rerun for this digest.
equations: Homogeneous root acceptance checks max|F_j/state_scale_j|<1e-6.
Interior thermal derivative uses [F(T-2h)-8F(T-h)+8F(T+h)-F(T+2h)]/(12h); inward stencils apply at physiological boundaries.
Positive biomass and acetate use softplus coordinates, logarithmic near zero; retained logarithms preserve uncensored per-capita dynamics.
Dense-output polynomial roots locate population minima, one-cell crossings and thermal extrema.

parameters.meaning: Absolute tolerances in pressure/biomass-coordinate/acetate-coordinate/ratio order, then temperature if present
parameters.units: mixed solver-coordinate units; K for T

parameters.value: rtol=2e-9; maximum step 2 yr; samples 0.5 yr

items.notes: Relevant regressions check source-shape transfers, independent break-even roots, budget conservation, four-chemistry Jacobians, the reference thermal crossing, exchange conservation, quadrature exactness, dial endpoints, unsafe-source rejection and census behavior. Historical main transient outputs used sampled accepted-source checks; four tighter controls added interval certificates. Current producer certification must not be attributed retrospectively to the old epoch. This task changed no files and used no web; R* values and unit conversions were independently recomputed.
